title: Rigveda 9.29: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.29: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.29 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 678v-679r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.29.1-2 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 678v
translation.original_text:
1prāsya̱ dhārā̍ akṣara̱n vṛṣṇa̍ḥ su̱tasyauja̍sā | de̱vām̐ anu̍ pra̱bhūṣa̍taḥ ||
2sapti̍m mṛjanti ve̱dhaso̍ gṛ̱ṇanta̍ḥ kā̱ravo̍ gi̱rā | jyoti̍r jajñā̱nam u̱kthya̍m ||
translation.text:
1FORWARD with mighty force have flowed the currents of this Steer effused, Of him who sets him by the Gods.
2The singers praise him with their song, and learned priests adorn the Steed, Brought forth as light that merits laud.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 678v (numbered 100v by the scribe) (OPenn image 679, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.27.5 ‹-hāsate pavamānaḥ adhi dyavi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 679r (numbered 101r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.29.3 ‹-tāni te punānāya prabhuvaso›. Verses 9.29.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1pra | asya | dhārāḥ | akṣaran | vṛṣṇaḥ | sutasya | ojasā | devān | anu | pra-bhūṣataḥ
2saptim | mṛjanti | vedhasaḥ | gṛṇantaḥ | kāravaḥ | girā | jyotiḥ | jajñānam | ukthyam

translation.original_ref: RV 9.29.3-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 679r
translation.original_text:
3su̱ṣahā̍ soma̱ tāni̍ te punā̱nāya̍ prabhūvaso | vardhā̍ samu̱dram u̱kthya̍m ||
4viśvā̱ vasū̍ni sa̱ṁjaya̱n pava̍sva soma̱ dhāra̍yā | i̱nu dveṣā̍ṁsi sa̱dhrya̍k ||
5rakṣā̱ su no̱ ara̍ruṣaḥ sva̱nāt sa̍masya̱ kasya̍ cit | ni̱do yatra̍ mumu̱cmahe̍ ||
6endo̱ pārthi̍vaṁ ra̱yiṁ di̱vyam pa̍vasva̱ dhāra̍yā | dyu̱manta̱ṁ śuṣma̱m ā bha̍ra ||
translation.text:
3These things thou winnest lightly while purified, Soma, Lord of wealth: Fill full the sea that claims our praise.
4Winning all precious things at once, flow on, O Soma, with thy stream Drive to one place our enemies.
5Preserve us from the godless, from ill-omened voice of one and all, That so we may be freed from blame.
6O Indu, as thou flowest on bring us the wealth of earth and heaven, And splendid vigour, in thy stream.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 679r (numbered 101r by the scribe) (OPenn image 679, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.29.3 ‹-tāni te punānāya prabhuvaso›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 679v (numbered 101v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.31.1 ‹svādhyaḥ pavamānāsaḥ akramuḥ rayim›. Verses 9.29.3-6 end on this page; 9.29.3 begins on fol. 678v (numbered 100v by the scribe).

4viśvā | vasūni | sam-jayan | pavasva | soma | dhārayā | inu | dveṣāṃsi | sadhryak
5rakṣa | su | naḥ | araruṣaḥ | svanāt | samasya | kasya | cit | nidaḥ | yatra | mumucmahe
6ā | indo iti | pārthivam | rayim | divyam | pavasva | dhārayā | dyu-mantam | śuṣmam | ā | bhara
